summary: Predicates as boxes with rational bounds. The meet of two boxes is their intersection; for a non-empty box 'every P is Q' is inclusion of bounds and is transitive; a contained predicate has no larger volume; 'every' implies 'most'; membership is positive degree; a comparative is a box; a union of two boxes need not be a box. Learning is modelled on a finite grid of candidate boxes with rational weights: after 'every V is M' and 'every M is R' an individual of V is in R with probability exactly 1, and after 'most P are Q' with threshold theta the probability is at least theta.

sources.citation: Bernardy, J.-P., Blanck, R., Chatzikyriakidis, S., Lappin, S. & Maskharashvili, A. (2019). Predicates as Boxes in Bayesian Semantics for Natural Language. NoDaLiDa 2019, pp. 333-337 (ACL Anthology W19-6137).

theorems.name: G1_certain
theorems.source_claim: G1_certain. If the quantity is 1 wherever the premises hold, its posterior expectation is 1.

theorems.name: G2_lower_bound
theorems.source_claim: G2_lower_bound. A lower bound that holds wherever the premises hold is a lower bound on the posterior expectation.

theorems.name: G3_syllogism_learned
theorems.source_claim: G3_syllogism_learned. Test suite T76, learned: under any prior over non-empty boxes, after observing "every V is M" and "every M is R", an individual of V is in R with probability exactly 1.

theorems.name: G4_most_learned
theorems.source_claim: G4_most_learned. After observing "most P are Q" with threshold theta, an individual of P is in Q with probability at least theta. The box counterpart of B7 in R3.

theorems.name: X1_meet_is_intersection
theorems.source_claim: X1_meet_is_intersection (2.1). The meet of two boxes is their intersection.

theorems.name: X2_every_is_inclusion
theorems.source_claim: X2_every_is_inclusion (2.2). For a non-empty box, the test on bounds is inclusion.

theorems.name: X3_every_transitive
theorems.source_claim: X3_every_transitive (3). "Every" is transitive. Test suite T76.

theorems.name: X4_inclusion_lowers_volume
theorems.source_claim: X4_inclusion_lowers_volume (3). A contained predicate has no larger volume.

theorems.name: X5_every_implies_most
theorems.source_claim: X5_every_implies_most (2.3). "Every" implies "most", for any threshold up to 1.

theorems.name: X6_degree
theorems.source_claim: X6_degree (2.4). Membership is positive degree, and the centre has degree 1. With it, test suite T15 holds in every box model: if Mary is tall and John is taller than Mary, then John is tall.

theorems.name: X7_comparative_is_box
theorems.source_claim: X7_comparative_is_box (2.4). "Taller than k" is a box: the same centre, with half-widths scaled by 1 minus the degree of k.

theorems.name: X8_union_is_not_a_box
theorems.source_claim: X8_union_is_not_a_box (2.5). Separation: a union of two boxes that is no box.

theorems.name: E_T76
theorems.source_claim: T76. All violinists are musicians; all musicians read music; so all violinists read music.

theorems.name: E_volumes
theorems.source_claim: The probabilities of the three predicates.

theorems.name: E_T77
theorems.source_claim: T77. ... so 99 percent of violinists read music.

theorems.name: E_T31
theorems.source_claim: T31, instantiation. John is a violinist; so John is a musician.

theorems.name: E_T15
theorems.source_claim: stated in the file; see its header

theorems.name: E_grid_size
theorems.source_claim: stated in the file; see its header

theorems.name: E_prior
theorems.source_claim: Before any observation: an arbitrary individual satisfies an arbitrary predicate with probability 1/2, and a P is a Q with probability 31/60.

theorems.name: E_premise_mass
theorems.source_claim: The premises themselves: "every P is Q" has prior probability 7/20, "most P are Q" (threshold 7/10) has 37/100.

theorems.name: E_posterior
theorems.source_claim: After observing "most P are Q": 73/74. After "every P is Q": 1.

theorems.name: E_contained_is_less_likely
theorems.source_claim: [BBCLM19] sec. 3: a predicate contained in another has a lower chance of holding of an arbitrary individual than an arbitrary predicate has. Here: 2/5 against the prior 1/2; the containing predicate rises to 7/10.

evidence: DRAFT for the author's review; not an accepted source-level verdict.
The paper's priors on box bounds and its sampling are replaced by a finite grid with exact weights.
Boxes are taken to lie in the unit box, where volume is probability. Negation is not formalized.

determination_rationale: DRAFT for the author. The geometry transposes directly; the learning results are a finite analogue.

artifact_classes.description: a finite grid of candidate boxes in place of continuous priors
a box as a list of lower and upper bounds; a negative width counts as 0
